findings.title: Add/remove member endpoints read group_id but routes set id
findings.body: add_members and remove_member both load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes are declared inside resources :groups the same way as put "suspend" on users (config/routes.rb delete/put "members"), so Rails registers member routes PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members and sets params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The admin client calls exactly /admin/groups/:id/members.json, so every add and remove raises ParameterMissing and returns 400 before any membership change. Controller specs inject group_id directly and never go through the router (the automatic-group remove example even uses xhr :put while the route is DELETE), so they stay green while the feature is broken in the browser.

findings.title: Public members page is stuck on the first 50 users
findings.body: findMembers always sends limit from the model default of 50, and the public group-members route only calls findMembers. group/members.hbs then renders that single page with no next/previous controls. Before this change, non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Any group larger than 50 now silently shows only the first page on the public members tab, so the rest of the membership cannot be viewed.

findings.title: Pager invents a blank page when count divides limit evenly
findings.body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so exactly 50 members with limit 50 is reported as 2 pages (100 members as 3, and so on). showingLast stays false on the real last page, and next() then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count. That request returns no rows, so the admin UI shows an empty extra page. Page count needs ceil division, and the next-page offset must be capped at the last page start, not at user_count.

findings.title: Invalid member offset is echoed and can 500
findings.body: members sets offset = params[:offset].to_i and limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no lower bound and no clamp to the last page, then returns that same offset in meta. The client copies meta.offset. Deleting the last user on the last page (51 members, limit 50, offset 50) therefore reloads an empty page and leaves offset at 50 even though total is now 50, so the admin pager stays on a blank page. A negative offset or limit is passed through to PostgreSQL, which errors with OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative and turns the request into a 500. Both values need to be clamped to >= 0, and offset past the end should rewind to the last page before the query.

findings.title: Remove link is shown for automatic groups
findings.body: group_member.hbs is rendered as an {{each}} itemView, so the template context is the member user, not the group. {{#unless automatic}} therefore looks up user.automatic, which is never set, and the remove control is always rendered. The add-members block in group.hbs correctly checks the group's automatic flag; this remove link does not. The server rejects membership edits on automatic groups with 422, and removeMember does not display that error, so the member looks removable and then simply stays in the list.

findings.title: Create ignores the alias level chosen in the form
findings.body: The admin form shows the alias-level combo box even before the group has an id, and the client asJSON payload includes alias_level on create. Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Unlike update, it never sets alias_level, so the first save stores the default (0, nobody) and drops whatever the admin selected. The value is only persisted if they open the group and save a second time.

findings.title: Membership add/remove failures are silent
findings.body: addMembers and removeMember fire the ajax calls and never handle rejection, unlike save which parses the response and shows bootbox.alert. addMembers also never clears the username field. On the server, unknown usernames are skipped one by one and add_members still returns 200, so a typo looks like a successful add that did not change the list. A 422 (automatic group) or a network error is an unhandled rejection with no message, and the filled input makes a retry resubmit the same names.

findings.title: Members endpoint does not cap page size
findings.body: limit is taken from the query string with only a default of 50 and no maximum. /groups/:name/members.json is available to anyone who can see the group, including very large automatic groups such as trust_level_0. A caller can pass limit=1000000 and force the process to load and serialize every member in one response. The new pagination API should clamp limit to a small maximum.

findings.title: Specs miss the route mismatch and the public members API
findings.body: The new membership examples call the controller actions directly with group_id, so they never notice that the routes expose params[:id]. The automatic-group remove example uses xhr :put, :remove_member even though the route is DELETE, which a request spec would not match. There is also no coverage of GroupsController#members: the new {members, meta} shape, the 50-row default, offset past the end, or negative limit/offset. Those gaps hide both the broken admin add/remove URLs and the public list truncation.
